requirements.description: Canonical schema-stamped Session envelopes are identical on disk and replay, with strictly monotonic per-Session sequence values and byte-stable framing.
Protocol framing rejects unsupported schemas, unsafe sequences, unknown or malformed events, non-canonical fields, and torn, empty, or multiple frames.
Initialize, Session lifecycle/subscription, Turn start/steer/interrupt, and approval resolve contracts expose the exact closed S1 method and decision vocabulary.
Subscribe sinceSeq and resume return exactly later durable envelopes and establish live delivery atomically without a replay/live gap or duplicate.
The filesystem semantic World assigns Session sequence authority, preserves append ordering across concurrent instances, filters replay boundaries, and lists validated Sessions.
Filesystem Session reads reject a partial or torn final NDJSON line without automatic ignore, truncation, or repair.
A headless faux-Provider Turn records the complete canonical Session-start, Turn, Step, model chunk/response, and Turn-end event trace.
Each model call receives explicit Session cache identity, cache retention, stable frozen system/tool prefix, and volatile history projected only from the Session log.
Provider errors and stream defects fail the Step/Turn without projecting a failed response into future model context, and no test accesses a real Provider or model.
Ready steer messages are durably recorded and folded into the next model call while stale expectedTurnId steering is rejected.
Turn starts received in flight queue one-at-a-time and automatically start in order only after current Turn finalization.
Interrupt targets only the expected active Turn, aborts in-flight work without fabricated results, and close safely rejects or releases runtime operations.
Parallel tool calls and internal before/after hooks execute concurrently while durable tool results are normalized and appended in source-call order; duplicate call IDs fail before execution.

The model-visible Memory tool performs batchable add, replace, and remove over exact delimited entries and rejects delimiter injection, malformed lists, missing matches, and ambiguous matches without writes.
MEMORY.md and USER.md limits count Unicode code points in final serialized state, accept the exact cap, and reject over-cap writes actionably without truncation or partial mutation.
Filesystem Memory batches commit both documents atomically and deterministic faults at every commit/recovery cut expose all-old or all-new state, never a mixed batch.

Session start persists one frozen assembled Memory snapshot; mid-Session writes are immediate but current prompts remain unchanged while a new Session observes new Memory, and resume uses the persisted snapshot without reading or recovering current Memory.
The filesystem composition runs a complete headless Turn, persists exact canonical envelopes, replays boundaries, freezes the executable Memory tool, and resumes replay plus live delivery atomically.
S1 scenarios emit bounded actual-runtime observations for canonical event traces, Provider inputs, fault schedules, and filesystem diffs into schema-validated redacted replay-bound evidence.

A separate Sol medium scout and independent reviewer record Session/Memory authority, loop ownership, ordering, atomicity, boundary-leak findings, and explicit dispositions in a retained evidence bundle.
